title: runtime-asks-interlock-and-low-effort-remediations-brief-2026-07-12
summary: Working synthesis of active customer feedback focused on runtime performance and small-surface product changes that unblock production usage. Emphasis on low-effort, high-impact remediations that CS can propose to customers as interim mitigations while engineering scopes larger fixes.
prioritized_requests: Request A — deterministic tail latency: several enterprise customers report 95th/99th token latency spikes with long chat histories; request: configurable hard-eviction policy for KV cache per-customer.
Request B — cost leakage on batch mixing: startups using mixed sequence-length workloads see inefficient batching; ask: a per-route batch-splitting hint or 'batch class' selector in route config.
Request C — embedding consistency: customers notice embedding drift across minor model refreshes; ask: ability to pin embedding model families and see diff metrics at rollout time.
Request D — observability gaps: token-level attribution for cost/latency not easily mapped to user flows; ask: 'session -> request -> token cost' trace aggregation export (CSV/BigQuery).
Request E — faster fallback path: when dedicated capacity is saturated, customers want a predictable fallback variant with capped latency rather than any auto-selected model that varies widely.
quick_win_actions: Enable a per-tenant KV cache TTL override (config flag) — small runtime toggle, low risk, addresses Request A partially; estimated eng effort: 3-5d.
Add a route-level 'preferred_batch_profile' tag (docs + SDK toggle) so CS can advise customers to isolate short/long workloads — estimated eng effort: 2-4d.
Publish an embedding-rollout checklist template in Console (docs + checkbox) that surfaces potential drift and required evals — product+docs ~2d.
Extend existing cost export to include 'session_id' column and a token-type label (prompt/completion/assist) for easier downstream joins — infra + analytics ~5d.
Introduce a 'stable-fallback' model alias in the model catalog that maps to a vetted low-latency variant with explicit SLOs; operational + catalog change ~3d.
engineering_notes: Notes to eng reviewers: these quick-wins assume existing knobs in the serving runtime (config flags, route metadata, catalog aliases). Key risks: per-tenant KV TTL could increase memory pressure if misused; propose safe defaults and a hard cap. For batch-tagging, ensure no regressions to existing automatic batching heuristics; implement as a hint rather than forcing. Cost export change touches analytics retention and billing; coordinate with finance for sampling policy.
customer_quotes: "We see occasional token storms on older chats — 200ms one minute then 1.2s the next. Our UX budget is tiny; we need predictable behavior." — B2B search startup (prod ops lead)
"When we rotated embedding model last month our semantic search drifted. We rolled back and froze for 6 weeks. Would help to have a safer rollout path." — Marketplace company (ML engineer)
"We get charged a lot for mixed-length batches; can't easily isolate high-cost flows. A simple route flag to keep short queries separate would be great." — Fintech scaling test (SRE)
"Exporting token-level cost tied to session IDs would make our internal chargeback painless. Right now we do manual estimation." — Platform team at enterprise customer
open_questions: Operational: What hard caps should we enforce if customers set very large KV TTLs? (memory/eviction policy implications)
Product: Should 'preferred_batch_profile' be exposed in the Console UI or only via API/route config initially?
Billing: Do we need approval from finance/legal before shipping finer-grained cost exports that make internal chargeback easier?
SLOs: What latency SLO should the 'stable-fallback' alias guarantee — 95th vs 99th, and across which sequence lengths?
next_steps: CS: run quick survey to 12 customers in our highest-usage cohort to validate which quick-wins would change their immediate behavior (due: 2026-07-19).
Product: decision meeting with eng+finance to greenlight cost-export fields (calendar invite: #product-runtime sync 2026-07-15).
Eng: spike ticket ENG-7690 to prototype per-tenant KV TTL flag with guardrails; deliver POC logs for CS by 2026-07-23.
Docs: draft a short 'interim-mitigation playbook' recommending combinations of the quick-wins for common customer archetypes; assign to Marco (due: 2026-07-20).
Follow-up: prepare an internal demo script to show customers trade-offs (latency vs cost vs memory) using synthetic workloads; aim for a customer webinar week of 2026-07-26.
